title: Calibration Technician (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR C4
raw_text:
9.     MOS 2871, Calibration Technician (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR C4

    a. Summary. Calibration Technicians are qualified to perform
calibration of mechanical, length, mass, and low complexity electronic Test
Measurement and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE) utilized within the Marine Corps.
Additionally, they are also trained to repair, modify, and make adjustments
that are routine in nature to TMDE as needed or required while under direct
supervision. Typical duties include the calibration and repair of
mechanical, length, mass, and low complexity TMDE while adhering to the
associated maintenance processes and metrology documentation established
within the appropriate references. Journeyman Calibration Technicians are
trained to perform the calibration of increasingly complex TMDE and
maintenance support equipment. Typical duties include the calibration,
troubleshooting, repair, modification, and adjustment of increasingly complex
TMDE, advanced level troubleshooting, and repairs of enterprise support
equipment. These technicians may also supervise ground maintenance
activities which include the execution of maintenance, maintenance
administration, MOS skill training, supporting quality control programs,
processing shipments of delicate TMDE to/from depot support, and assisting
with the deployment/employment of the calibration facility. These
technicians assist with the associated maintenance management and metrology
requirements outside of a routine nature. Marines in this MOS may be
assigned to a BIC (within their occupational field) that has been coded with
one or more DoD cyber workforce framework (DCWF) work role codes. Please
reference DoDI 8140.10, DoDM 8140.10, and the MOS roadmap for additional
training and certification requirements associated with these work role
codes.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must have normal color vision.

            (3) Must possess an EL score of 110.

            (4) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

        (5) Must have completed one year of high school Algebra 1, Integrated
Mathematics, Mathematical Studies SL or an equivalent course at the minimum.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Must complete the Calibration Technician Course (M3028T1) at
Keesler AFB, MS.

        (2) Marines must have 36 months obligated service remaining upon
graduation from the Calibration Technician Course. This obligated service
must be obtained prior to execution of PCS (DUINS) or PCA (DUINS) orders to
the course.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (q), 2800 Ground Electronics Maintenance Training and Readiness
Manual.




                                           3-259                        Enclosure (1)
 3124                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Precision Instrument and Equipment Installers and Repairers, All Others 49-
9069.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.
common_text: The Ground Electronics Maintenance Occupational Field includes the installation, inspection and classification, servicing, adjustment, tuning, repair, modification, recovery and evacuation, overhauling and rebuilding, and testing and calibration of electronic equipment and systems used by Marine Corps ground forces. The equipment includes various types of communications transmission systems, information technology systems, intelligence processing systems, tactical sensor systems, cryptographic devices, artillery electronics systems, digital fire control systems, unmanned vessel electronics, miscellaneous non-communication systems, robotic and various electro-mechanical systems, electronic jamming systems, and a wide range of test equipment and calibration required devices. Qualifications to work in this field include manual dexterity, normal color vision, be eligible to hold a secret security clearance, the ability to understand highly technical material, and to comprehend complex mathematical and logic principles. Types of entry-level jobs available include work as a Ground Electronics Transmission Systems Maintainer, Ground Electronics Telecommunications and Information Technology Systems Maintainer, Calibration Technician, Artillery Electronics Technician, and Digital Wideband Systems Maintainer. Formal schooling is provided to all Marines entering this field. In general, entry-level training consists of basic electronics, electronic systems fundamentals, and an equipment-oriented phase at either a Marine Corps school or other service school. Career progression training will involve related supervisory/technical level training within the field. Skill progression, skill enhancement and skill sustainment training is provided via on the job training and through both distributed learning and formal schooling. Billets for ground electronics maintenance are found throughout the Marine Corps but are concentrated within units having specific electronic or service support missions. Marines in this field may serve within GCE, ACE, MLG, MIG units and supporting establishments. Instructor billets are found at the formal schools responsible for ground electronics training. Marines entering this field will be assigned MOS 2800, Basic Ground Electronics Maintenance Marine.

matches: Modify, maintain, or repair electronics equipment or systems to ensure proper functioning.

The Ground Electronics Maintenance Occupational Field includes the installation, inspection and classification, servicing, adjustment, tuning, repair, modification, recovery and evacuation, overhauling and rebuilding, and testing and calibration of electronic equipment and systems used by Marine Corps ground forces.
Supervise maintenance of telecommunications equipment.

Types of entry-level jobs available include work as a Ground Electronics Transmission Systems Maintainer, Ground Electronics Telecommunications and Information Technology Systems Maintainer, Calibration Technician, Artillery Electronics Technician, and Digital Wideband Systems Maintainer.
Supervise or train other technologists, technicians, or drafters.
Career progression training will involve related supervisory/technical level training within the field.
Install, service, and repair electronic equipment or instruments such as televisions, radios, and videocassette recorders.
Billets for ground electronics maintenance are found throughout the Marine Corps but are concentrated within units having specific electronic or service support missions.
Teach courses within their department.
Instructor billets are found at the formal schools responsible for ground electronics training.
Conduct calibration tests to determine performance or reliability of mechanical, structural, or electromechanical equipment.

Calibration Technicians are qualified to perform calibration of mechanical, length, mass, and low complexity electronic Test Measurement and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE) utilized within the Marine Corps.
Train new repairers.
Additionally, they are also trained to repair, modify, and make adjustments that are routine in nature to TMDE as needed or required while under direct supervision.
Maintain or repair measurement devices or equipment used for calibration testing.

Typical duties include the calibration and repair of mechanical, length, mass, and low complexity TMDE while adhering to the associated maintenance processes and metrology documentation established within the appropriate references.
Calibrate, validate, or maintain laboratory equipment.
Journeyman Calibration Technicians are trained to perform the calibration of increasingly complex TMDE and maintenance support equipment.
Calibrate, troubleshoot, or repair equipment and correct malfunctions, as needed.

Typical duties include the calibration, troubleshooting, repair, modification, and adjustment of increasingly complex TMDE, advanced level troubleshooting, and repairs of enterprise support equipment.
Supervise maintenance of telecommunications equipment.

These technicians may also supervise ground maintenance activities which include the execution of maintenance, maintenance administration, MOS skill training, supporting quality control programs, processing shipments of delicate TMDE to/from depot support, and assisting with the deployment/employment of the calibration facility.
Perform routine repair and maintenance duties.
These technicians assist with the associated maintenance management and metrology requirements outside of a routine nature.
Perform maintenance tasks necessary to keep equipment working properly.
For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (q), 2800 Ground Electronics Maintenance Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
